title: Unicode strings
description:
Write these text functions. They must work for any language, not just ASCII:

```rust
fn capitalize_words(text: &str) -> String       // "élan VITAL" gives "Élan Vital"; words separated by single spaces in the result
fn is_palindrome(text: &str) -> bool             // ignoring case and anything that is not alphanumeric
fn truncate(text: &str, max_chars: usize) -> String   // at most max_chars characters; if cut, the last one is "…"
fn run_lengths(text: &str) -> String             // "aaabcc" gives "a3bc2"; works on characters, not bytes
fn reverse_words(text: &str) -> String           // "one two  three" gives "three two one"
```

`truncate("Grüße aus Köln", 6)` is `"Grüße…"`; if the text fits, it is returned unchanged; `max_chars` 0 gives `""`.
hints: Never slice a string at an arbitrary number of bytes: count and take characters with `chars()`, which handles letters like `ü` and emoji that take several bytes.
`c.to_uppercase()` returns an iterator (some characters become several), so collect it into a `String`; `chars.as_str()` gives the rest of the word after the first character.
